public_rationale: He forecast that AI agents will eventually do a huge share of knowledge work and be worth trillions, and he explicitly said 'no time soon'. In October 2025, the best agent on the Remote Labor Index automated only 2.5% of real freelance projects. That matches his near-term caution but does not test the long-term forecast. With no deadline and no decisive event, the claim stays open.
limitations: 'Worth trillions' is not tied to a specific metric.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Eventually, though not soon, AI agents will do a huge fraction of human knowledge work, perhaps physical labor too, and be worth trillions.

statement.excerpt: And they will be worth trillions, since eventually (no time soon) they will do a huge fraction of all human knowledge work, and maybe physical labor too.
statement.document_title: AI Agents: Hype versus Reality, redux

from_speaker: they will do a huge fraction of all human knowledge work
our_interpretation: Read as an undated long-term forecast: AI agents will eventually do a large share of human knowledge work and create economic value in the trillions of dollars.
'Maybe physical labor too' is hedged, so it is not part of the test.
'No time soon' means near-term evidence cannot contradict it.
criteria.support_condition: Credible labor or economic data show agents doing a large share of knowledge work, with economic value or market value in the trillions of dollars.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No fixed deadline. Only a decisive, lasting failure of agents to do much knowledge work over a very long period would count against it.
